evidence: Cic. Off. 1.28: aut labōrem aut sūmptūs suscipere nōlunt
terms.comment: Of a task, a burden, an expense, a war, taken on of one’s own accord; recipere is used of a task one is given or has promised (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: undertake, take on (a duty, a promise); guarantee
evidence: Cic. Div. Caec. 26: mihi Siculōrum causam receptam, populī Rōmānī susceptam esse videor (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Its first sense is to take back; in sē recipere, to take upon oneself (see undertake responsibility).
Also to approach someone, and to attack.
Not found in Lewis & Short or the loci collections in this form; Traupman is the only evidence. The classical verbs are suscipere and recipere (above).

phrases.latin: Nam aut inimīcitiās aut labōrem aut sūmptūs suscipere nōlunt
phrases.english: for they are unwilling to take on enmities, or work, or expense

sources: Lewis & Short: suscipio · Lewis & Short: recipio · Lewis & Short: aggredior
